title: Amihan Wind
tagline: A 60 MW onshore wind farm in Luzon, Philippines. The sponsor is asking for a USD 69.75m senior loan.
tutorialHint: Look at the whole life of the loan, and at the whole bank.

blocks.text: Tax is ignored: the project benefits from an income tax holiday.

Luzon needs every megawatt of clean power it can get, and spot prices on the wholesale market have risen for three years in a row. We will re-contract at the same level or better. Our solar portfolio was financed over 18 years by two other banks; we expect the same here.
The sponsor's base case uses our P90. We have no concerns on the yield.

The selected turbine is certified for typhoon-class winds (IEC class T) and has more than ten years of operating history in Taiwan and Japan. Insurance quotes include typhoon damage and business interruption.

The full-service agreement covers the first 5 years of operation, including the manufacturer's warranty and a 97% availability guarantee. The USD 1.8m per year in the business plan reflects that price. From year 6, once the warranty ends, we estimate USD 3.0m per year for a comparable scope: scheduled and unscheduled maintenance, major component replacement and higher insurance premiums.

items: Plant design, EPC contract and grid connection: sound, no concerns.

Spot prices have been high since 2023, but more than 6 GW of solar and wind is planned in Luzon by 2035. We expect prices captured by wind plants to soften from the mid-2030s. Lenders should not rely on a re-contracting price above our low case.

onStart.text: Hi, Amihan is Northpoint's first wind project and they want to bring us their whole Luzon pipeline if this goes well. Their solar portfolio got 18 years elsewhere, so they expect the same from us. Term sheet by Friday, and please keep the documentation light, they found our last requests heavy.

committeeClosing.text: Thank you. The committee will deliberate. You'll hear from us shortly.

decisions.label: Approve as requested
decisions.hint: Lend the amount and tenor requested, on the sponsor's terms.

decisions.label: Approve with conditions
decisions.hint: Change the amount and add conditions to protect the bank.

conditions.label: DSRA of 6 months funded at close
conditions.reason: Six months of debt service set aside in cash: a buffer for a bad year.

conditions.label: Dividend lock-up below 1.20x DSCR
conditions.reason: Cash stays in the project instead of going to the sponsor if the DSCR falls.

conditions.label: Syndicate the amount above USD 45m to another bank
conditions.reason: Needed: it is the only way to lend more than the USD 45m the bank can hold.
conditions.redundantReason: Not needed: the loan is already within the USD 45m the bank can hold.

conditions.label: Full KYC on all direct and indirect shareholders above 10% before signing
conditions.reason: Covers Silverbay (25%, indirect, no identified owner). Required before signing, it does not stop the approval.

conditions.label: Standard KYC on Northpoint Energy, the listed parent
conditions.reason: Not enough: it does not cover the 25% shareholder in the British Virgin Islands.

conditions.label: Allow dividend payments from year 1, whatever the DSCR
conditions.reason: The opposite of a lock-up: cash leaves the project even when the DSCR falls.

conditions.label: Comfort letter from Northpoint on re-contracting the PPA after year 12
conditions.reason: A comfort letter is not binding: it does not secure any revenue after year 12.

committee.question: The PPA ends after year 12. What price did you assume for years 13 to 18, and how did it shape the tenor you propose?
committee.goodAnswer: The market study's low case, 6.0 cents, not the sponsor's 7.6. At that price an 18-year loan falls to a 0.99x DSCR from year 13, against 1.50x required on merchant revenues. So the tenor stops at 12 years, the end of the PPA, which also supports more debt: USD 58m.

committee.question: Are the operating costs in the business plan realistic for the whole life of the loan?
committee.goodAnswer: No: USD 1.8m only covers the 5-year warranty period. The engineer expects USD 3.0m from year 6, which brings the cash flow down to USD 9.78m and the maximum debt to USD 58m.

committee.question: Can we hold this loan on our balance sheet?
committee.goodAnswer: Not all of it: the loan counts against the Northpoint group limit, since Northpoint owns 75% of the borrower. USD 155m is already used out of USD 200m, so USD 45m is available. Hold USD 45m and syndicate the rest, or lend less.

committee.question: Northpoint won't say who is behind Silverbay, their 25% partner. They say Northpoint is listed, so KYC on Northpoint should be enough. Can we accept that and close on Friday?
committee.goodAnswer: No. Silverbay holds 25% indirectly and its beneficial owner is unknown; KYC on the listed parent does not cover it. Full KYC on all shareholders above 10% is required before signing. It does not stop the approval: offer to help them provide it quickly so we can still close.

right.label: Approve with the right conditions
right.story: The deal closes. In 2034 the O&M contract is renewed at USD 3.1m; the DSCR holds above 1.30x. Northpoint brings its next wind project to the bank.

limit.label: Sent back by Portfolio Management
limit.story: Priya Nair refuses to sign off: holding more than USD 45m would breach the group limit. The deal goes back to the drawing board and misses Friday.

compliance.label: Blocked by Compliance
compliance.story: Two days before signing, Compliance freezes the deal: Silverbay's owner was never identified. The sponsor is furious and the case reaches the Head of Credit.

lost.label: Lost to competitor
lost.story: Northpoint finds the term sheet too heavy and signs with another bank. Kevin reminds everyone about the pipeline.

approve.label: Approve as requested
approve.story: The request passes every check as it stands.

decline.label: Decline
decline.story: A competitor finances the project. Northpoint takes its pipeline elsewhere.

risk.label: Rejected by Risk
risk.story: Margaret Chen sends the proposal back: on the bank's own case it breaks the credit policy (DSCR below 1.30x on contracted years or 1.50x on merchant years, gearing above 75%, or more than 2 years of tenor beyond the PPA).

conservative.label: Too conservative
conservative.story: Your offer is far below what the bank could lend within policy. Northpoint takes the whole pipeline to a bank that offered more, and Kevin asks why we left money on the table.

outcomeContext: The consequence appears a few cases later, when the O&M contract comes up for renewal.

spotted: The PPA ends after 12 years, but the loan runs 18. The sponsor assumed the same price forever; the market study's low case is 6.0 cents, and policy requires 1.50x on merchant revenues. Over 18 years the DSCR falls to 0.99x from year 13.
The USD 1.8m of operating costs only covers the 5-year warranty. From year 6 the engineer expects USD 3.0m.
The loan counts against the sponsor's group limit (Northpoint owns 75% of the borrower): only USD 45m is available, whatever the DSCR.
A 25% shareholder in the British Virgin Islands has no identified owner. KYC on the listed parent does not cover it.
debrief.summary: The fix: a 12-year tenor (which supports the most debt, USD 58m), the bank's share capped at USD 45m with the rest syndicated, and full KYC before signing.
debrief.lesson: A good project is not automatically a good loan. Look at the whole life of the debt, and at the whole bank.

answerKey.summary: The project is sound in its first years, but the sponsor's case hides two step-downs in cash flow, and two bank-side constraints apply whatever the DSCR. As requested (USD 69.75m over 18 years), the deal fails all four tests.

traps.title: Trap 1 — PPA shorter than the debt
traps.text: The PPA runs 12 years, the loan 18. The sponsor assumes the same 7.6 cents after year 12. The market study's low case, recommended for lenders, is 6.0 cents from the mid-2030s. On the bank case, the DSCR falls to 0.99x from year 13, against 1.50x required on merchant revenues, and the bank accepts at most 2 years beyond the PPA. Cutting the tenor to 12 years removes the merchant tail and supports the most debt: USD 58.2m.

traps.title: Trap 2 — Operating costs after the warranty
traps.text: The USD 1.8m per year only holds for the 5-year full-service agreement. The engineer expects USD 3.0m from year 6. On its own the trap is discreet (DSCR 1.36x from year 6 at USD 69.75m), but it cuts the maximum debt over 12 years from USD 65.3m to USD 58.2m.

traps.title: Trap 3 — Single-group exposure
traps.text: The bank already lends USD 155m to the Northpoint group, against a USD 200m limit, and this loan counts against it because Northpoint owns 75% of the borrower. The bank can hold at most USD 45m, whatever the DSCR. The rest must be syndicated to another bank, or the loan reduced.

traps.title: Trap 4 — Incomplete KYC
traps.text: A 25% indirect shareholder (Silverbay, British Virgin Islands) has no identified beneficial owner. KYC on the listed parent alone does not cover it. Full KYC on all direct and indirect shareholders above 10% must be a condition before signing. It does not stop the approval, only the signing.

rightDecision.title: Right decision: approve with conditions
options: Debt sized within policy on the bank case, with a tenor of 14 years at most: USD 58.2m at most over 12 years (the most debt), less over shorter or longer tenors. Over 12 years at USD 58m: debt service USD 7.50m, DSCR 1.30x, gearing 62%, sponsor equity USD 35.0m.
The bank's share capped at USD 45m: syndicate the rest, or lend USD 45m only.
Full KYC on all direct and indirect shareholders above 10% before signing.

answerKey.extraCredit: Conditions that earn extra credit: the 6-month DSRA funded at close (about USD 3.8m at USD 58m over 12 years) and a dividend lock-up below 1.20x DSCR.
answerKey.weakAnswers: Weak answers: an 18-year loan (more than 2 years beyond the PPA: Risk rejects it), a loan sized on the sponsor's prices, holding more than USD 45m without syndication, a loan far below what policy allows (the sponsor walks away), a comfort letter instead of real structure, dividends allowed whatever the DSCR, or KYC on the listed parent only.

best.note: The bank's best answer: the bank case in the control center (merchant price about 6.0, operating costs about 3.0 from year 6), a tenor within the PPA (12 years supports the most debt: USD 58.2m, DSCR 1.30x, gearing 63%), USD 45m held and the rest syndicated, and full KYC before signing. Up to 2 years beyond the PPA (13 or 14 years) is also accepted, but supports much less debt (USD 40.1m at most over 14 years); beyond that, Risk rejects it.

tenor.offNote: More than 2 years beyond the 12-year PPA: the bank does not take that much merchant risk, so Risk rejects it.
